owner_posts.post_text: The energy, the milestones, and the moments that made the Agents’ Carnival ’26 at Valluvar Kottam Auditorium truly special. We came together to celebrate 20 glorious years of service, packed with inspiring leadership talks, dynamic cultural shows and a lot more. Watch the video to catch the best highlights, leadership insights, and high-energy performances from the event!

Close to 5,000 residents. Over 140 doctor consultations. More than 1,700 diagnostic tests. 100+ vaccinations. All free. All in Nashik.

Star Health has operationalised an Arogya Seva Kendra in Nashik, in partnership with Piramal Swasthya, offering primary healthcare services free of cost to the community.

"Good health often begins with timely access to basic healthcare services," said Mr. HIMANSHU WALIA, Whole-time Director and Chief Marketing Officer, Star Health and Allied Insurance. "Through Arogya Seva Kendras, we are helping ensure individuals and families can access consultations, screenings and preventive care closer to where they live, without financial barriers."

Star Health has always believed that Insurance is more than a claim. It is a partnership with the communities where our policyholders live, work, and raise their families.

Across Maharashtra, we operate 5 Arogya Seva Kendras. Nationally, the programme runs 32 centres across 9 states, all aimed at improving primary healthcare access in underserved communities.

Early Detection. Better Health. Healthy Tomorrow.

Star Health's CFO has been recognised at the 9th BW CFO World (BW CFO World Best CFO & Finance Strategy Excellence Awards) 2026, held on 9 June at Novotel Andheri, Mumbai.

Best CFO (Large Enterprise), Silver- awarded to Mr. Nilesh Kambli, who has been the financial backbone of Star Health through its FY26 milestones.

Excellence in Financial Transformation, Silver- awarded to Star Health Insurance, the only health insurer recognised in the category. The recognition reflects Star Health's shift to a digital-first finance and customer operations stack. Over 1 million customers used Star Health's digital health services in FY26 alone.

The awards were evaluated by a jury chaired by Mr. Ravi S former Chairman, BSE, and presented in the presence of Mr. Adv. Ashish Shelar Cabinet Minister, Government of Maharashtra.

Behind every Silver is a finance team building the rails for the next Gold.

BW Businessworld

hashtag#StarHealthInsurance hashtag#StarHealth hashtag#HealthInsurance hashtag#Award

In 2006, Star Health and Allied Insurance became India's first standalone Health Insurance company. Twenty years later, the launch of Value Plus marks the next chapter, and India's leading publications carried the story.

The Economic Times, covered Star Health's two-decade milestone alongside the launch of Value Plus.

Value Plus is an affordable Health Insurance offering designed to bring wider health protection to young Indians in Tier 2, 3 and 4 cities at nearly 20% lower premiums. It offers high sum-insured covers from ₹7.5 lakh to ₹25 lakh through a curated network of 11,000+ quality hospitals.

20 years in. The next chapter begins now.

"Insurance growth in India is no longer a metro story. The next wave will come from Tier II, Tier III and Tier IV markets.”

In an interview with Shine Jacob from Business Standard, our MD and CEO Anand Roy laid out why retail health penetration in smaller towns is non-negotiable for the country's Insurance for All by 2047 vision.

The first 20 years helped build India's health insurance category. The next 20 will be about taking protection deeper into Bharat.

"GWP up to ₹5,968 crore. Net profit up to ₹111 cr."

That was the headline takeaway in The Economic Times, on Star Health and Allied Insurance's Q4 FY26 results.

The coverage walked through the company's Q4 numbers. Net profit at ₹111 crore, a multi-fold jump from ₹50 lakh in the same quarter last year. Net Premium at ₹5,599 crore, up from ₹4,820 crore YoY. Total income at ₹4,545 crore, up from ₹3,989 crore YoY. And the underwriting loss narrowed sharply to ₹154 crore from ₹275 crore in the year-ago period.

Star Health has launched 32 Arogya Seva Kendras (ASK) under its CSR initiative to strengthen access to community-level primary healthcare across nine states, with the goal of impacting over one million lives.

In partnership with Piramal Swasthya (part of Piramal Foundation), these clinics will provide free primary healthcare services, including:

* MBBS doctor consultations
* Screening for hypertension, diabetes, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs)
* Laboratory diagnostics and essential medicines
* Health counselling and awareness sessions
* Adult pneumococcal vaccination support, with expertise from Pfizer

With hypertension prevalence ranging from 20–40% and diabetes affecting up to 29% of adults in certain districts, this initiative highlights the urgent need for preventive and accessible primary care to address India’s growing NCD burden.

A meaningful step toward healthcare equity ensuring quality primary care reaches communities early, consistently, and close to home.

Star Health reported strong Q3 FY26 performance, supported by premium growth, disciplined underwriting, and improved operating efficiency.
The quarter reflects sustained focus on profitability, claims excellence, and customer trust.

featured_reviews.name: Sarona D Sa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience with Star Health Insurance.

I have been trying to close my policy for over a month now. I raised multiple tickets through the app, but they were repeatedly closed without any proper resolution or clear explanation.

I am an NRI and currently living outside India, so it is not possible for me to visit a branch office in person. To make things worse, the Star Health app does not function properly outside India, which makes it even more difficult to manage or close my policy.

When I contacted my agent for assistance, he initially responded but later completely stopped replying to my WhatsApp messages and never completed the cancellation process. Being ignored while trying to close a policy is extremely unprofessional.

I was also told that I could not update my bank details after closing my bank account and would instead need to cancel my existing policy and purchase a new one — which meant losing the premium rate I had previously locked in. This was very frustrating.

On top of that, my gender was incorrectly reflected in the app, and despite following up multiple times, it was never corrected.

The lack of accountability, poor communication, and unresolved issues have made this a very stressful experience. Based on my experience, I would not recommend Star Health Insurance.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear  Sarona D Sa ,

We’re sorry to hear about your experience. Kindly share more information regarding your concern to support@starhealth.in or call our helpline @ 1800-425-2255. Our concerned department will connect with you in resolving your issue.

Team Star Health

featured_reviews.name: Nitesh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been policyholders for 4 years with continuous premium payments. Despite this, our claim during a genuine medical emergency involving gastroenterology and kidney complications was denied.

Even after medical reconsideration was submitted by the treating doctor, the claim was rejected again without transparent reasoning. Due to claim delays, we were forced to shift hospitals, yet the insurer continued denying coverage.

This conduct reflects unfair claim practices and lack of accountability. If this matter is not addressed properly, we will escalate it to IRDAI and other appropriate regulatory authorities.

Insurance is meant to provide protection during emergencies, not create additional stress for families already dealing with medical crises.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Rate Zero

I bought the Max Bupa Policy to get extra comfort and flexibility and paid higher & extra premium compared to other policies. I was told that I would get Health check up complimentary ( restricted to very few tests depending upon your age slab)...You are asked to select a medical centre from the list provided to you from your neighbourhood, which is unheard of places...the preliminary idea of getting a excellent & class medical centre is shattered here..and we are forced to select a some unknown ones. Next shock, you have to write an email to the company of your appointment time & date, and they will send you the voucher with the printed & fixed conditioned time & date of that centre by post or courier.
By that time it reaches you, any of you or your family has any other change in personal schedule, you cannot change it. Its gone... the time is gone. One has to go through the entire process once again. The company believes it is giving all this complimentary, so we are not to say anything, we are slave to their policy conditions since it is free.. We as customer, know the free cost is included in our higher premiums.
Next shocker, shopping vouchers ! The so said free shopping vouchers are not coming to you as it is. You are supposed to select the brand you want to shop, and give the outlet's details by email. The voucher with the outlet's & the brand name will arrive at your door step in next 10-12 days.. By the time you want a particular item from that brand, if it is not available by now ( after 10-12 days), the voucher is good for nothing or you end up buying unwanted as your next choice. The process is there to re-apply again...but why can't they send simple vouchers with value printed and ask us to select from the list of dealers they give? Sorry, its free, so no help! All free things from them cannot be questioned for the logistics attached to each free & complimentary services..!
I dread to think of my family if it were to really claim medical insurance during my hospitalisation.
I will recommend readers or intending purchasers to ponder a bit and research and then buy the policy (with freedom and flexibility) offered by Max-Bupa.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Beri
featured_reviews.review_text:
The New India Assurance Building is a striking architectural gem located at 87, Mahatma Gandhi Road in the historic Fort district of Mumbai, India. Completed in 1937 and designed by the firm Master, Sathe and Bhuta, with artistic input from N. G. Pansare, this six-story office structure stands as a prime example of Art Deco architecture with an Indian twist — often described as Indo-Deco.  
Wikipedia +1
What immediately captivates visitors is its bold façade, characterized by pronounced vertical ribs that create a sense of grandeur and height, despite the building’s moderate scale. At street level, detailed bas-relief sculptures depict scenes of everyday life — Indian farmers, industrial workers, and traditional attire — seamlessly blending local culture with the streamlined geometric forms of Art Deco. These artistic reliefs don’t just decorate the building; they narrate India’s social and economic spirit during the pre-independence era.  
Wikipedia +1
The design also reflects an early appreciation for climate-responsive architecture. Projections on the east and west façades help shield windows from direct sunlight, and operable windows allow airflow — thoughtful features for Mumbai’s tropical environment long before modern HVAC systems were commonplace.  
Around Us
Design aficionados and heritage lovers regard the New India Assurance Building as a key component of the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble of Mumbai, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Its aesthetic appeal lies not just in ornamentation but in how it communicates confidence, modernity and Indian identity at a time when corporate architecture was often dominated by colonial European styles.  
Wikipedia
Inside, the building continues to function as an office — it serves as a headquarters for the New India Assurance Company Ltd, a long-established insurance provider founded in 1919 by Sir Dorabji Tata that has grown into one of India’s biggest general insurers.  
New India
In summary, the New India Assurance Building is far more than an ordinary office block. It’s a cultural and architectural landmark that captures a unique historical moment — where global design trends met indigenous expression — and continues to be appreciated by historians, architects, and everyday passersby in Mumbai’s bustling Fort area.

featured_reviews.name: ANKIT KUMAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am extremely disappointed with Care Health Insurance. My experience has revealed a massive gap between their promises and their actual service, particularly when it comes to renewals versus new sales.
1. The "Sales vs. Support" Trap
It is incredibly easy to reach their sales team—they will call you back in seconds if they think they’re getting a new premium. However, the moment you need help with a renewal or have a technical issue, they become ghosts. Trying to get a human on the line to discuss renewal terms is a nightmare, and the "support" is practically non-existent compared to the aggressive energy of their sales department.
2. The "30% Renewal Discount" is a Scam
Don’t be fooled by their marketing about earning a 30% discount on renewals via their app. I followed all the rules and installed the Care Health app to track my steps. They require you to hit a 10K step goal, which I did.
However, the app is fundamentally broken:
The step counter stays at default or fails to sync properly.
Even though I was active and met the criteria, the app didn't recognize my progress.
Because their own buggy software failed to track my data, they are now refusing to honor the discount.
3. Consumers Pay for Their Technical Failures
As a consumer, I am now facing the consequences of their technical incompetence by being forced to pay a higher premium. It feels like a "bait and switch" tactic—lure you in with the promise of health-based discounts that are impossible to actually claim because the tracking system is rigged to fail
